scope: Requirement-to-test mapping, not a claim that the full release evidence has passed.

basic.title: a supplied basic Process compiles to the agreed design-time meaning

missingFlow.title: a dangling Sequence Flow is refused with its missing reference identified

flowDirection.title: an End Event cannot send a Sequence Flow back into a Start Event

unknownConcept.title: an unimplemented semantic feature is refused instead of silently omitted

flowScope.title: a Sequence Flow cannot cross its Process scope

duplicate.title: duplicate semantic keys never become ambiguous XML identities

xor.title: an Exclusive decision preserves a condition and its explicit default path

default.title: a default Sequence Flow belongs to its owner and never carries a condition

parallel.title: parallel work retains both branches and its explicit synchronization

inclusive.title: an Inclusive split preserves independently applicable branch conditions

illegalCondition.title: events and Parallel Gateways cannot acquire conditional Sequence Flows

decisionCondition.title: a decision split requires stated conditions or an explicit default

primary.title: the requested primary model must resolve before any XML is emitted

blackBox.title: a collaboration can preserve a message between two black-box participants

sendTask.title: a white-box participant sends a declared Message through a Send Task

receiveTask.title: a Receive Task preserves a declared incoming Message

missingMessage.title: a communication task cannot silently discard an unresolved Message reference

messageScope.title: Message Flows cross participant boundaries and never connect internal work

missingCollaborationRef.title: collaboration references never disappear during serialization

messageEndpoint.title: Message Flow endpoints must be interaction nodes, not control routing or None Events

nestedLanes.title: nested lanes retain responsibility with derived ancestor membership

laneMembership.title: lane membership has one leaf owner and cannot assert a competing ancestor assignment

laneParent.title: lane parent chains must resolve to an acyclic same-Process scope

ambiguousParticipant.title: a multiply instantiated Process never silently chooses its Message Flow participant

taskTypes.title: task classifications preserve design-time meaning without invented engine configuration

loops.title: standard and multi-instance repetition retain exactly the stated design-time loop semantics

subprocess.title: embedded Subprocess flow and responsibility remain nested independent of presentation

recursiveContainment.title: recursive Subprocess containment is refused without dropping a disconnected scope

nestedFlow.title: a Sequence Flow cannot shortcut from a parent into its Subprocess

call.title: a Call Activity references an explicit same-file Process QName without copying its contents

missingCall.title: a Call Activity cannot hide an unresolved external process reference

illegalLoop.title: loop markers cannot be silently accepted on non-Activity nodes

namespace.title: semantic projection treats a default BPMN namespace and its equivalent prefix identically

expertLane.title: expert invalid lane inspection preserves a resolvable foreign reference instead of omitting it

messageEvents.title: Message Events retain their named payload and boundary interruption in every supported position

signalEvents.title: Signal Events preserve named broadcast meaning in catching, throwing, and boundary positions

timerEvents.title: Timer Events retain exactly one inert timer expression in each legal placement

conditionalEvents.title: Conditional Events preserve the supplied business condition without an execution binding

illegalTrigger.title: event triggers cannot be moved into illegal throwing or embedded-start positions

eventRefs.title: boundary attachments and named Event references resolve without silent substitution

eventFlow.title: events and gateways cannot claim legal control flow when their required connections are absent

eventGateway.title: Event-Based Gateways preserve competition and explicit instantiating variants

illegalEventGateway.title: event-based configurations refuse illegal targets, instantiation, and receive-message mixing

nonePlacement.title: None Events stay within the profile Start and End positions

messageAgreement.title: named communication references agree and intermediate Message Events do not fan out messages

errorEvents.title: Error Events preserve named throws and interrupting named or catch-all boundaries

escalationEvents.title: Escalation Events preserve ordinary continuation and either explicit boundary interruption choice

terminateEvents.title: Terminate End Events retain their enclosing scope without converting the parent completion

illegalException.title: exception Events require legal positions, named throws, and interrupting Error catches

linkEvents.title: same-scope Link continuation derives stable definition references without inventing Sequence Flows

illegalLink.title: Link continuation refuses unmatched names, multiple catches, cross-scope matching, and flow shortcuts

entry.title: an explicit End Event requires explicit entry while entirely eventless scopes remain legal

dataRefs.title: Data Objects, States, and Data Stores retain distinct stable references and capacity semantics

dataScope.title: data artifact references and lifecycle scope cannot silently resolve to another kind or a child lifetime

processActivityIO.title: Process and Activity IO preserve declarations with complete derived input and output sets

eventIO.title: Events use direct catching outputs and throwing inputs instead of an Activity IO specification

illegalIO.title: IO declarations enforce legal owners, direction, and named communication cardinality

dataAssociations.title: Data Associations retain owner-specific input and output meaning with exact IO references

illegalDataAssociation.title: Data Associations require typed, accessible endpoints and the owning IO while expert mode retains multiple sources

associationRoles.title: Data Associations check each endpoint role even when the same key occurs twice

eventDataAssociations.title: catching and throwing Event Data Associations retain their real XML placement and direction

documentation.title: intentional annotations, groups, categories, and associations remain standard non-control-flow artifacts

illegalDocumentation.title: documentation artifacts refuse dangling references and unsafe owners without inventing category or labels

unnameable.title: the compiler never accepts nonstandard names on unnameable documentation or data association elements

input.title: the full Consulting Core record families travel through structured input without coercion or loss

badInput.title: malformed input, unsupported versions and unknown top-level fields are refused without payload disclosure

inputBounds.title: input budgets apply to the whole invocation before large or deeply nested content is accepted

history.title: identities and evidence references are unambiguous while deleted identities remain reserved

labels.title: empty optional text is omitted and conditional-flow labels reuse the supplied condition without replacing explicit names

deferredFamilies.title: XSD-valid Deferred BPMN families remain explicit limitations without a replacement model

deferredVisual.title: Deferred visual concepts refuse rendering while inert nonvisual extension data remains an explicit profile limitation

execution.title: execution payloads, formal resources, vendor attributes and multiple Event definitions remain explicit unsupported content

executionAttributes.title: unmapped standard execution attributes cannot silently pass the design-time profile

executionIO.title: optional and alternative IO-set execution configuration cannot disappear into simple design-time IO records

suppliedLink.title: explicit supplied Link references must agree with their same-scope continuation meaning

suppliedData.title: the generated data and intentional-documentation families retain valid semantics and supplied DI through external inspection

xsd.title: the official local XSD distinguishes legal Definitions from a missing required namespace

renderBasic.title: rendering returns a readable self-contained deterministic SVG of the supplied diagram

renderBlackBox.title: a black-box-only collaboration has truthful pool and message geometry

renderLanes.title: nested lanes keep their assigned activities visually contained

renderShared.title: two participants sharing one Process remain visible without cloned process meaning

renderCall.title: same-file call targets are rendered as complete additional panels

renderCollapsed.title: collapsed subprocess contents have a complete separate panel

renderExpanded.title: explicitly expanded subprocesses contain their contents on the parent panel

renderMessage.title: message events retain catching, throwing and non-interrupting boundary notation

renderIO.title: Process-level Data Input and Output receive native visible DI and labels

renderDataAssociation.title: Activity IO stays complete in XML while data associations dock on its visible owner

renderTimerConditionalSignal.title: timer forms, conditional waits and signal throws retain native event geometry

variant.activity-classifications.title: generation renders Script and Receive Task classifications with their native symbols

variant.event.link.continuation.title: generation preserves same-scope Link continuation with catching and throwing symbols

requirements.description: Definitions: target namespace, one self-contained document, stable IDs
Process: explicit design-time nonexecution, same-file definitions
Collaboration: one primary subject with Participants and Message Flows
White-box Pool references a same-file Process
Black-box Pool retains absent internal work
Lane and derived nested Lane responsibility
Embedded Subprocess, collapsed with separate contents panel
Call Activity same-file QName target without copied process
Sequence Flow same-scope legal node references
Human-readable condition expression with preserved explicit label or normalized fallback
Default belongs to its Activity/Gateway and never has a condition
Exactly one inert Timer expression: timeDate
Exactly one inert Timer expression: timeDuration
Exactly one inert Timer expression: timeCycle
Inter-participant named Message Flow without implicit participant selection
Named Message declaration references in Tasks, Events and Flows
Data Object with stable Data Object Reference and State
Visible Process IO with derived input/output sets
Catching outputs and throwing inputs directly under Events
Global persistent Data Store, capacity/unlimited and named state references
Activity Data Association, exact owner/input/output/source/target semantics
Event Data Association with catching/throwing direction
Category-backed Group; geometry-only memberRefs, cross-pool grouping
Standard Association with None/One/Both direction, never Data Association substitution
Item definitions and external data schemas
Vendor namespaces, metadata, listeners and eBPMN
Retained semantic identities, reserved historical identities and bounded closed input
One explicit primary Process or Collaboration with same-file references
isExecutable=false and no invented engine behavior
Intentional standard documentation only; no automatic statuses or metadata
Reference kinds, same-file QName namespace equivalence and safe scope
Recoverable invalid meaning retained without unsafe reference omission

remainingEvidence: Run ten fresh notation executions for every applicable feature-slice case, not only composition fixtures.
Bind full CORE-01 through CORE-07 evidence to the exact clean candidate and package hashes.
The visual mappings identify executable checks, not recorded outcomes; bind their actual results to the exact candidate before qualification.
Run cross-platform semantic/identity/DI comparison and full clean-install checks.
Record all eight composition human reviews; source/expected rows are authored synthetic facts, not human review evidence.
Complete host, handoff, offline runtime, safety, scale and performance gates in their separate acceptance runners.
